Requirement: All tailoring shall be evaluated for use by the KSC Engineering Directorate Technical Authority (see KSC-PLN-5400).
Model issues: The requirement is too vague; 'evaluated for use' lacks a measurable criterion.
How to verify: Review the generated evaluation report against the criteria defined in KSC-PLN-5400.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall provide an evaluation report for all tailoring, conforming to the criteria specified in KSC-PLN-5400.

Requirement: Waivers to institutional requirements shall follow the process in KDP-KSC-P-1865.
Model issues: The requirement relies on an external document (KDP-KSC-P-1865) which is not defined here, making verification dependent on external knowledge.
How to verify: Inspect the waiver documentation to confirm adherence to the process outlined in KDP-KSC-P-1865.
Suggested rewrite: Waivers to institutional requirements shall follow the process defined in KDP-KSC-P-1865.

Requirement: Conflicts between this standard and applicable documents cited herein shall be resolved by the responsible Technical Authorities.
Model issues: The requirement delegates resolution authority without defining the resolution process or criteria, making it untestable.
How to verify: Review the system design documentation to confirm that the most stringent requirement is prioritized during conflict resolution.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall adhere to the most stringent requirement when conflicts exist between this standard and applicable documents cited herein.

Requirement: COTS equipment shall be evaluated for acceptability from a materials and processes (M&P) standpoint (see 6).
Model issues: The requirement lacks a clear subject performing the action (who evaluates the equipment?).
How to verify: Review the evaluation documentation to confirm the responsible party assessed the COTS equipment against the criteria in section 6.
Suggested rewrite: The <<Responsible Party>> shall evaluate COTS equipment for acceptability from a materials and processes (M&P) standpoint per section 6.

Requirement: Qualification tests and inspections shall be indicated in the engineering documentation.
Model issues: The term 'indicated' is vague; it needs to specify *how* the indication must occur (e.g., via a specific field, flag, or section).
How to verify: Review the engineering documentation to confirm the presence of records for all qualification tests and inspections.
Suggested rewrite: The engineering documentation shall include a record of all qualification tests and inspections.

Requirement: Vendor documentation shall be provided as evidence that the requirements of this standards manual have been met.
Model issues: The requirement is too vague regarding what constitutes 'evidence' and how the documentation must be provided.
How to verify: Review the provided vendor documentation against the standards manual requirements.
Suggested rewrite: The vendor shall provide documentation demonstrating compliance with the requirements of this standards manual.

Requirement: Modifications to COTS shall be performed in accordance with this standards manual.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a clear subject performing the action.
How to verify: Inspect the modification documentation to confirm adherence to the standards manual.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall perform modifications to COTS in accordance with this standards manual.

Requirement: The GS design shall support the program/project-specific operational requirements of flight hardware.
Model issues: The requirement is too vague; 'support' and 'program/project-specific operational requirements' are not measurable.
How to verify: Inspect the GS design documentation against the requirements listed in <<document reference>>.
Suggested rewrite: The GS design shall implement all operational requirements specified in <<document reference>>.

Requirement: GS shall not degrade or contaminate flight systems, other GS, subsystems, or experiments while it is being used, checked out, serviced, or otherwise handled.
Model issues: The term 'degrade' is not quantifiable; it needs a measurable threshold or failure mode.; The term 'contaminate' is not quantifiable; it needs a defined contamination metric or boundary.
How to verify: Monitor the specified systems during operation and handling to confirm no measurable degradation or contamination occurs.
Suggested rewrite:
GS shall not cause any measurable degradation to flight systems, other GS, subsystems, or experiments while it is being used, checked out, serviced, or otherwise handled.
GS shall not introduce any measurable contamination to flight systems, other GS, subsystems, or experiments while it is being used, checked out, serviced, or otherwise handled.

Requirement: GS design shall include access provisions for handling, servicing, calibrating, maintaining, and replacing components and limited-life items.
Model issues: The scope of 'access provisions' is too broad; specify the required level or type of access.
How to verify: Inspect the design drawings to confirm the presence of specified access provisions for each listed activity.
Suggested rewrite:
The GS design shall provide access provisions for handling components.
The GS design shall provide access provisions for servicing components.
The GS design shall provide access provisions for calibrating components.
The GS design shall provide access provisions for maintaining components.
The GS design shall provide access provisions for replacing components and limited-life items.

Requirement: GS shall meet the requirements of all interfaces with new or existing hardware or software as documented in interface control documents (ICDs) or any other documentation that controls interface requirements.
Model issues: The requirement is too broad and relies on external, undefined documentation to define its scope.
How to verify: Review the ICDs and verify that GS implementation matches the documented interface requirements.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall comply with all interface requirements specified in the Interface Control Documents (ICDs).

Requirement: Fluid, mechanical, or electrical connections in close proximity shall be designed to prevent cross-connections.
Model issues: The term 'close proximity' is not quantified, making verification impossible.
How to verify: Inspect the design drawings to confirm that separation distances meet the specified <<distance>>.
Suggested rewrite: Fluid, mechanical, or electrical connections shall be designed to prevent cross-connections when located within <<distance>>, and this design shall be verifiable via inspection.

Requirement: GS shall be compatible with all facility interfaces.
Model issues: The term 'all facility interfaces' is too broad and not verifiable without a defined set of interfaces.
How to verify: Inspect the GS against the documented interface specifications.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall be compatible with the interfaces defined in <<Interface Specification Document>>.

Requirement: GS shall be designed for the operational life specified by program or mission requirements and identified in design drawings and maintenance documents.
Model issues: The requirement references external documents ('program or mission requirements', 'design drawings and maintenance documents') without specifying how the operational life shall be determined or what the resulting value is.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm the specified operational life has been incorporated into the GS design.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall be designed for an operational life of <<specified operational life>>.

Requirement: Existing GS that was verified to meet the GS requirements of a previous NASA program shall be considered acceptable for use without further verification to the requirements of this standards manual.
Model issues: The term 'acceptable' is not measurable and needs a specific criterion for acceptance.
How to verify: Inspect the existing GS against the criteria documented in the acceptance criteria document.
Suggested rewrite: Existing GS verified to meet the GS requirements of a previous NASA program shall be accepted for use without further verification if it meets the criteria defined in <<acceptance criteria document>>.

Requirement: Items with limited life shall be identified on design drawings and annotated with the specific limitation to the life of the item.
Model issues: The term 'identified' is vague; specify the required method of identification.
How to verify: Inspect the design drawings to confirm that all items with limited life are marked and annotated with their specific life limitation.
Suggested rewrite: Items with limited life shall be marked on design drawings and annotated with the specific limitation to the life of the item.

Requirement: The colors in Appendix A shall be used for GS designed and painted for NASA/KSC.
Model issues: The term 'GS designed and painted' is too vague; specify the exact object or system this applies to.
How to verify: Inspect the physical object against the color standards listed in Appendix A.
Suggested rewrite: The colors specified in Appendix A shall be used for <<specific object/system>> designed and painted for NASA/KSC.

Requirement: Redundant systems, subsystems, or components shall be physically oriented or separated such that the failure of one will not prevent the other from performing its intended function.
Model issues: The term 'physically oriented or separated' is too vague to verify without defining the required separation distance or orientation criteria.
How to verify: Measure the physical distance between the redundant components and confirm it meets the specified minimum separation distance.
Suggested rewrite: Redundant systems, subsystems, or components shall maintain a physical separation distance of <<minimum separation distance>> to prevent the failure of one from preventing the other from performing its intended function.

Requirement: Redundant systems, subsystems, or components shall be designed such that common- cause failures (e.g., contamination) do not eliminate redundancy.
Model issues: The term 'designed such that' is too abstract; it needs a measurable design constraint or verification method.
How to verify: Review the system design documentation to confirm the implementation of specified common-cause failure mitigation features.
Suggested rewrite: Redundant systems, subsystems, or components shall incorporate design features that prevent common-cause failures (e.g., contamination) from eliminating redundancy.

Requirement: The design of redundant systems shall provide methods for verifying each redundant element without compromising the reliability of the redundant system.
Model issues: The term 'methods for verifying' is too vague; specify the required verification mechanism or criteria.
How to verify: Review the system design documentation to confirm the existence of a verification mechanism for each redundant element.
Suggested rewrite: The design shall provide a mechanism to verify each redundant element without compromising the reliability of the redundant system.

Requirement: GS, except primary structure and pressure vessels/piping/tubing in rupture mode, shall be designed to sustain a failure without causing loss of life or damage to support equipment, facilities, or flight hardware (fail-safe).
Model issues: The term 'fail-safe' is a design philosophy, not a verifiable requirement; it needs to be quantified by defining the acceptable consequence of the failure.
How to verify: Analyze the failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) against the defined safety criteria.
Suggested rewrite: GS, except primary structure and pressure vessels/piping/tubing in rupture mode, shall sustain a failure without causing loss of life or damage to support equipment, facilities, or flight hardware, provided the failure consequence meets the defined safety criteria of <<safety level>>.

Requirement: GS shall be designed to sustain a failure and still perform its basic function (fail- operational) when necessary to meet safety or operational requirements.
Model issues: The term 'basic function' is not defined and must be specified.
How to verify: Analyze the system design documentation to confirm the defined basic function is maintained following a specified failure mode.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall sustain a failure and still perform its basic function when necessary to meet safety or operational requirements.

Requirement: GS failure modes/inadvertent operator actions with the potential for loss of flight crew shall be addressed in accordance with NPR 8705.2.
Model issues: The requirement is too high-level and references an external document without defining the specific actions or outcomes required.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm compliance with NPR 8705.2 regarding GS failure modes and operator actions.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall address GS failure modes and inadvertent operator actions with the potential for loss of flight crew in accordance with NPR 8705.2.

Requirement: GS shall be designed such that failures will not be propagated to the flight systems.
Model issues: The term 'failures' is too broad; specify the types of failures to be prevented from propagation.
How to verify: Review the system architecture and failure mode analysis to confirm that specified failure types are isolated from the flight systems.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall prevent the propagation of <<specific failure types>> to the flight systems.

Requirement: A criticality assessment shall be performed early in the design phase to determine the need for performing a reliability and/or safety analysis.
Rule findings: and/or: and/or; passive voice: shall be performed
Model issues: The timing 'early in the design phase' is too vague; specify a milestone or phase gate.
How to verify: Review the design documentation to confirm the criticality assessment was performed at the specified milestone.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall perform a criticality assessment at <<design phase milestone>> to determine the need for performing a reliability analysis or a safety analysis.

Requirement: System inputs (including dependencies such as electrical power and pneumatic purges) and outputs (including all control and monitoring functions) that could fail with potentially catastrophic or critical consequences shall be identified as reliability critical (FMEA is required).
Rule findings: open-ended list: such as; absolute: all
Model issues: The requirement bundles identification, classification, and process mandate (FMEA).
How to verify: Review the system design documentation and FMEA report to confirm all critical items are identified and classified.
Suggested rewrite:
The system shall identify all inputs and outputs that could fail with potentially catastrophic or critical consequences.
These identified inputs and outputs shall be classified as reliability critical.
An FMEA shall be performed on all reliability critical components.

Requirement: Systems with hazards to personnel or equipment during normal or credible use scenarios shall be identified as critical (Hazard Analysis is required).
Model issues: The term 'normal use scenarios' needs to be quantified or defined.
How to verify: Review the hazard analysis documentation to confirm that all systems with identified hazards in defined operational scenarios are marked as critical.
Suggested rewrite: Systems with hazards to personnel or equipment during defined operational scenarios shall be identified as critical (Hazard Analysis is required).

Requirement: An FMEA shall be performed in accordance with program-defined methodology on those systems and subsystems identified by the criticality analysis as having the potential to cause a criticality 1, 1S, 1R, or 2 condition.
Model issues: The phrase 'in accordance with program-defined methodology' is too vague; the specific methodology must be referenced or defined.
How to verify: Review the performed FMEA document to confirm it adheres to the specified methodology and covers all identified critical systems.
Suggested rewrite: An FMEA shall be performed on systems and subsystems identified by the criticality analysis as having the potential to cause a criticality 1, 1S, 1R, or 2 condition, using the <<specific FMEA methodology document/standard>>.

Requirement: Based on the results of the FMEA, components having failure modes that could cause an undesirable event (other than criticality 3) shall be identified, categorized, and approved in accordance with the applicable agency, program, or KSC requirements.
Model issues: The requirement is too broad; it needs to specify *how* the identification, categorization, and approval processes must occur.
How to verify: Review the documentation to confirm that the identified, categorized, and approved components meet the specified agency, program, or KSC requirements.
Suggested rewrite: Components with failure modes that could cause an undesirable event (other than criticality 3) shall be identified, categorized, and approved according to the applicable agency, program, or KSC requirements.

Requirement: In the absence of a program requirement, the methodology of KNPR 8700.2 shall be used.
Model issues: The phrase 'In the absence of a program requirement' is conditional and needs to be tied to a specific trigger or state for verification.
How to verify: Inspect the system configuration or documentation to confirm the use of KNPR 8700.2 when no program requirement is present.
Suggested rewrite: If no program requirement is specified, the system shall use the methodology defined in KNPR 8700.2.

Requirement: The criticality categories shown in Table 1 shall be used when the program does not identify categories.
Model issues: Table 1 must be referenced to define the criticality categories.
How to verify: Inspect the system documentation and configuration to confirm the use of Table 1 categories when program identification fails.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall use the criticality categories defined in Table 1 when the program does not identify categories.

Requirement: Static components, such as pressure vessels, pressure lines, cables, connectors, and wiring, shall be considered only if failure can be attributed to an active component failure.
Model issues: The condition for considering static components is unclear; it needs a specific criterion for attributing failure to an active component.
How to verify: Review the failure analysis documentation to confirm that the failure mode was traced to an active component.
Suggested rewrite: Static components, including pressure vessels, pressure lines, cables, connectors, and wiring, shall be considered for failure analysis only if the failure mode can be demonstrably traced to a failure in an active component.

Requirement: A Hazard Analysis shall be performed on those systems and subsystems determined by the criticality assessment to be a potential threat to flight systems, ground systems, or safety.
Model issues: The term 'potential threat' is too vague and needs a measurable criterion or scope definition.
How to verify: Review the criticality assessment documentation to confirm which systems and subsystems were included in the Hazard Analysis.
Suggested rewrite: A Hazard Analysis shall be performed on systems and subsystems determined by the criticality assessment to be a threat to flight systems, ground systems, or safety.

Requirement: Based on the results of the Hazard Analysis, those hazards that could not be eliminated by design or mitigated to an acceptable level shall require a Hazard Report.
Model issues: The term 'acceptable level' needs a quantifiable threshold or reference standard.
How to verify: Review the Hazard Analysis documentation to confirm the risk level against the defined threshold.
Suggested rewrite: Hazards that cannot be eliminated by design or mitigated to a risk level of <<acceptable risk level>> shall require a Hazard Report.

Requirement: FMEA and/or Hazard Analysis including the results of the analysis shall be combined into a Systems Assurance Analysis (SAA) to summarize the risks resulting from each system/subsystem analysis.
Model issues: The requirement bundles two distinct actions: combining analyses and summarizing risks.
How to verify: Review the final SAA document to confirm it contains the combined FMEA and Hazard Analysis results and a risk summary for each subsystem.
Suggested rewrite:
The system shall combine the FMEA results into the Systems Assurance Analysis (SAA).
The system shall combine the Hazard Analysis results into the Systems Assurance Analysis (SAA).
The SAA shall summarize the risks resulting from each system/subsystem analysis.

Requirement: CIL and Hazard Reports shall be approved and maintained as part of the design documentation.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a specific actor responsible for approval and maintenance.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm the presence and approval status of the CIL and Hazard Reports.
Suggested rewrite:
The <<Responsible Party>> shall approve CIL and Hazard Reports.
The <<Responsible Party>> shall maintain CIL and Hazard Reports as part of the design documentation.

Requirement: GS shall be designed to perform in the natural and induced environments to which it will be subjected during its life cycle.
Model issues: The requirement is too vague; 'natural and induced environments' must be specified.; The requirement lacks a measurable criterion for 'perform'.
How to verify: Review the design documentation against the specified environmental envelope.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall operate within the specified environmental envelope defined in <<Environmental Specification Document>>.

Requirement: GS used or stored in an uncontrolled exterior environment shall be designed to function after exposure to the natural environment at its respective geographical location as specified in NASA-HDBK-1001.
Model issues: The phrase 'designed to function after exposure' is vague; it needs a specific performance metric or operational state to verify functionality.
How to verify: Subject the GS to environmental conditions specified in NASA-HDBK-1001 and verify that it maintains specified operational performance.
Suggested rewrite: GS used or stored in an uncontrolled exterior environment shall maintain specified operational performance after exposure to the natural environment conditions defined in NASA-HDBK-1001.

Requirement: GS required to function during or after exposure to the launch-induced environment shall be designed to withstand the environment defined in program-specific documents.
Model issues: The phrase 'shall be designed to withstand' is too vague; it needs a specific performance metric or standard to verify the design.
How to verify: Review the design documentation against the environmental specifications in the program-specific documents to confirm compliance.
Suggested rewrite: The GS shall maintain specified functionality when exposed to the launch-induced environment defined in program-specific documents.

Requirement: Testing of GS for launch-induced environment shall be applied in accordance with KSC-STD-164.
Model issues: The requirement is passive and lacks a clear subject responsible for the action.
How to verify: Inspect the test plan to confirm adherence to KSC-STD-164 for GS launch environment testing.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall test GS for launch-induced environment in accordance with KSC-STD-164.

Requirement: GS not required to function after exposure to the launch-induced environment shall not cause damage or create a hazard to flight hardware, facilities, other GS, personnel, or the environment.
Model issues: The requirement bundles multiple outcomes (damage to hardware, facilities, other GS, personnel, environment) into a single negative statement.; The term 'cause damage or create a hazard' is too broad and lacks measurable criteria.
How to verify: Expose the GS to the launch-induced environment and inspect all listed items for damage or hazard creation.
Suggested rewrite:
The GS shall not cause damage to flight hardware upon exposure to the launch-induced environment.
The GS shall not create a hazard to facilities upon exposure to the launch-induced environment.
The GS shall not create a hazard to other GS upon exposure to the launch-induced environment.
The GS shall not create a hazard to personnel upon exposure to the launch-induced environment.
The GS shall not create a hazard to the environment upon exposure to the launch-induced environment.

Requirement: GS designed to function within a controlled interior environment shall be designed to the following temperature and humidity requirements:
Model issues: The requirement lacks specific numerical values for the temperature and humidity limits.
How to verify: Place the system in a chamber set to the specified temperature and humidity and verify operation.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall operate within a controlled interior environment where the temperature shall be between <<min temp>> and <<max temp>> and the relative humidity shall be between <<min humidity>> and <<max humidity>>.

Requirement: GS shall be designed to meet the program/project contamination control requirements.
Model issues: The requirement is too vague; 'meet the program/project contamination control requirements' needs to be quantified or referenced to a specific, verifiable standard.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm adherence to the specified contamination control requirements.
Suggested rewrite: GS shall comply with the contamination control requirements specified in <<document ID>>.

Requirement: Clean rooms and associated controlled environments designated as GS shall be designed in accordance with ASTM E2217.
Model issues: The term 'designated as GS' is vague; specify the criteria for designation.
How to verify: Review the design documentation to confirm compliance with ASTM E2217 for environments designated as GS.
Suggested rewrite: Clean rooms and associated controlled environments shall be designed in accordance with ASTM E2217 when designated as GS.

Requirement: GS used in an uncontrolled interior environment shall be designed to meet the most severe exterior environmental conditions for humidity and temperature expected at the respective geographical locations, as defined in NASA-HDBK-1001.
Model issues: The requirement is too broad; it needs to specify *which* environmental conditions (humidity/temperature) must be met, rather than just referencing a document.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation to confirm the specified environmental limits from NASA-HDBK-1001 are incorporated into the GS design.
Suggested rewrite: The GS shall be designed to meet the maximum humidity and temperature conditions specified in NASA-HDBK-1001 for the respective geographical locations.

Requirement: If GS will be operated in locations where fire or explosion hazards exist, as defined by NFPA 70, Article 500, it shall be hazardproofed in accordance with the requirements in KSC-STD-E-0002.
Model issues: The condition 'If GS will be operated in locations where fire or explosion hazards exist' is conditional and needs a clear trigger or state to verify the requirement.
How to verify: Inspect the GS documentation and physical installation to confirm compliance with KSC-STD-E-0002 when operating in a designated hazardous location.
Suggested rewrite: If the operating environment meets the definition of a fire or explosion hazard per NFPA 70, Article 500, the GS shall be hazardproofed in accordance with KSC-STD-E-0002.

Requirement: Environmental methods and conditions required for testing and qualification of GS components shall be in accordance with MIL-STD-810 and KSC-STD-164.
Model issues: The requirement is too broad; it should specify which specific methods/conditions from the standards apply, or if the entire standard must be followed.
How to verify: Review the test plan to confirm that all environmental testing procedures reference the specified standards.
Suggested rewrite: The testing and qualification of GS components shall comply with the environmental methods and conditions specified in MIL-STD-810 and KSC-STD-164.

Requirement: GS used in Zones 3 or 4 as defined in NASA-HDBK-1001 shall be designed to resist the effects of a seismic event using the criteria and guidelines in ASCE-7.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a specific performance criterion (e.g., survival, operational capability) when subjected to the seismic event.
How to verify: Review the design documentation against ASCE-7 criteria to confirm the specified performance level is met.
Suggested rewrite: GS used in Zones 3 or 4 as defined in NASA-HDBK-1001 shall be designed to resist the effects of a seismic event according to the criteria and guidelines in ASCE-7, achieving <<specific performance level>>.

Requirement: Drawings and specifications required for the fabrication, construction, installation, modification, test, operation, maintenance, sustaining, and use of GS shall be prepared in accordance with drawing practices equal to or more stringent than the engineering drawing practices of ASME Y14.100 and KSC-GP-435, Vol.
Model issues: The requirement references an incomplete standard reference (Vol.)
How to verify: Inspect the documentation against the specified drawing practices to confirm compliance with the referenced standards.
Suggested rewrite: Drawings and specifications for the fabrication, construction, installation, modification, test, operation, maintenance, sustaining, and use of GS shall be prepared in accordance with drawing practices equal to or more stringent than the engineering drawing practices of ASME Y14.100 and KSC-GP-435, Vol. <<placeholder>>.

Requirement: Technical documentation (e.g., manuals and reports) shall be prepared in accordance with KSC-DF-107.
Model issues: The requirement is too broad; it should specify *what* documentation must be prepared (e.g., 'The system shall generate technical documentation...').
How to verify: Inspect the prepared documentation against the KSC-DF-107 standard.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall prepare technical documentation in accordance with KSC-DF-107.

Requirement: GS design documentation shall identify spare parts, components, materials, and items necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.
Model issues: The requirement bundles multiple distinct identification tasks (spare parts, components, materials, items) into one statement.
How to verify: Review the GS design documentation to confirm the presence of identified lists for spare parts, components, materials, and items.
Suggested rewrite:
The GS design documentation shall identify spare parts necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.
The GS design documentation shall identify components necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.
The GS design documentation shall identify materials necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.
The GS design documentation shall identify items necessary to support construction, fabrication, installation, activation, test, verification, and operation.

Requirement: Limited-life items shall be controlled from the date of their manufacture through their period of operational use, including the time they are in storage.
Model issues: The term 'controlled' is not defined; specify the control mechanism (e.g., tracking, inventory management).
How to verify: Inspect the inventory tracking system records to confirm the start and end dates of control for selected limited-life items.
Suggested rewrite: Limited-life items shall be tracked from the date of manufacture through their period of operational use, including storage time.

Requirement: The status of limited-life items shall be documented.
Model issues: The requirement lacks specificity regarding what 'documented' means (e.g., format, location, required data fields).
How to verify: Inspect the <<documentation system>> to confirm the status of limited-life items is recorded.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall record the status of limited-life items in <<documentation system>>.

Requirement: GS design documentation shall identify limited-life items and provide instructions for replacement of those parts, components, and materials.
Model issues: The requirement bundles two distinct actions: identification and providing replacement instructions.
How to verify: Inspect the GS design documentation to confirm the presence of identified limited-life items and corresponding replacement instructions.
Suggested rewrite:
GS design documentation shall identify limited-life items.
GS design documentation shall provide instructions for replacement of identified limited-life parts, components, and materials.

Requirement: All components used in critical GS shall undergo qualification to verify performance in their intended environment in accordance with KSC-STD-G-0003.
Model issues: The term 'critical GS' is undefined and needs to be specified.
How to verify: Review the component qualification documentation to confirm adherence to KSC-STD-G-0003 for all components within the specified critical GS.
Suggested rewrite: All components used in <<critical GS>> shall undergo qualification to verify performance in their intended environment in accordance with KSC-STD-G-0003.

Requirement: GS design shall incorporate quality requirements in accordance with the program’s/project’s S&MA Plan.
Model issues: The term 'incorporate quality requirements' is too vague; specify *how* they must be incorporated.
How to verify: Inspect the GS design documentation against the S&MA Plan to confirm compliance with all specified quality requirements.
Suggested rewrite: GS design shall comply with all quality requirements specified in the program’s/project’s S&MA Plan.

Requirement: Quality requirements shall be defined on the engineering drawings or in other technical documents that are included in the design, fabrication, or installation contract.
Model issues: The requirement is too broad; it states *where* quality requirements shall be defined rather than *what* the quality requirements are.
How to verify: Review the design, fabrication, and installation contracts to confirm the presence of documented quality requirements.
Suggested rewrite: Quality requirements shall be documented in the engineering drawings or in other technical documents included in the design, fabrication, or installation contract.

Requirement: Certification documentation for required training of personnel performing processes during fabrication, assembly, installation, and testing of GS shall be maintained in accordance with KNPR 8730.2.
Model issues: The requirement is passive and could be clearer regarding who is responsible for maintenance.
How to verify: Inspect the documentation repository to confirm the presence and adherence of training records to KNPR 8730.2.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall maintain certification documentation for personnel training related to fabrication, assembly, installation, and testing of GS in accordance with KNPR 8730.2.

Requirement: Testing requirements shall be specified in engineering documentation.
Model issues: The term 'engineering documentation' is too broad; specify which documents must contain the testing requirements.
How to verify: Review the specified engineering documentation to confirm the presence of testing requirements.
Suggested rewrite: Testing requirements shall be specified in <<specific engineering documentation>>.

Requirement: Testing shall verify compliance with the applicable specifications and the ability of the GS to perform its required design functions.
Model issues: The requirement is too broad; it combines verification scope (compliance) with functional capability testing.
How to verify: Execute a test plan covering all specified functions and compare results against expected outcomes.
Suggested rewrite:
The system shall comply with all applicable specifications.
Testing shall verify that the GS performs its required design functions.

Requirement: Test documentation, data, and results shall be produced, maintained, and archived in accordance with KNPR 8730.2 and program or project requirements.
Model issues: The requirement bundles three distinct actions (produce, maintain, archive) that should likely be separated for clarity.
How to verify: Inspect the documentation, maintenance logs, and archive structure to confirm adherence to KNPR 8730.2 and project requirements.
Suggested rewrite:
Test documentation shall be produced in accordance with KNPR 8730.2 and program or project requirements.
Test documentation shall be maintained in accordance with KNPR 8730.2 and program or project requirements.
Test documentation shall be archived in accordance with KNPR 8730.2 and program or project requirements.

Requirement: A load test shall be performed on all structural GSE (access platforms, workstands, etc.) and moveable or articulating GS structures except when the load test creates an unsafe condition or when analysis shows the load test will result in damage to the structure.
Rule findings: open-ended list: etc; absolute: all; passive voice: shall be performed
Model issues: The scope is too broad ('all structural GSE... and moveable or articulating GS structures') and the exclusion criteria are conditional and non-testable.; The requirement bundles the action (load test) with complex, non-testable exceptions.
How to verify: Review the documented list of structures and the documented criteria for load test exclusion.
Suggested rewrite:
The system shall define a specific list of structural GSE and moveable/articulating GS structures subject to load testing.
For each structure on the list, the system shall perform a load test unless the test creates an unsafe condition or analysis predicts structural damage.

Requirement: The minimum test load shall be 125% of the design or working load for GS not used for lifting.
Model issues: The term 'design or working load' needs to be defined or referenced to be verifiable.
How to verify: Review the system documentation to confirm the defined design or working load value.
Suggested rewrite: The minimum test load shall be 125% of the <<design or working load>> for GS not used for lifting.

Requirement: Lifting devices and equipment shall be proofload tested in accordance with NASA-STD-8719.9.
Model issues: The requirement relies on an external standard (NASA-STD-8719.9) which may not be fully accessible or applicable without context; specify the required test outcome or acceptance criteria if the standard is not universally known.
How to verify: Perform the proofload test on the lifting devices and equipment following the procedures in NASA-STD-8719.9 and confirm the load is sustained for the specified duration without failure.
Suggested rewrite: Lifting devices and equipment shall be proofload tested in accordance with NASA-STD-8719.9, and the test shall demonstrate the device can support a load of <<load magnitude>> for a duration of <<duration>>.

Requirement: In the absence of design analysis, a load test of 8 times the safe working load shall satisfy the factor of safety requirements of this standards manual.

How to verify: Measure the depth of the removed layer on a sample piece and confirm it meets the specified minimum depth.
Suggested rewrite: The surfaces of titanium and titanium alloy mill products shall be 100% machined, chemically milled, or pickled to a depth of <<minimum depth>> to remove all oxygen-contaminated layers formed as a result of mill processing, heat treating, and forming operations at elevated temperatures.

Requirement: All cleaning fluids and other chemicals used during manufacturing and processing of titanium hardware shall be verified to be compatible with and not detrimental to the material’s performance.
Rule findings: absolute: All; passive voice: shall be verified
Model issues: The requirement lacks a specific criterion for 'compatible with and not detrimental to the material’s performance'.
How to verify: Review the chemical compatibility test reports against established material performance standards.
Suggested rewrite: The manufacturing process shall verify that all cleaning fluids and other chemicals used are compatible with titanium hardware and do not detrimentally affect the material’s performance.

Requirement: Copper alloys, brasses, and bronzes that are resistant to general corrosion and pitting, and highly resistant to SCC in accordance with MSFC-STD-3029 shall be used in GS.
Model issues: The requirement bundles material selection criteria (corrosion resistance, SCC resistance) with a specific standard reference (MSFC-STD-3029) without defining the required performance level or scope of the standard's application.
How to verify: Inspect material certifications and documentation to confirm compliance with MSFC-STD-3029.
Suggested rewrite:
The materials used in GS shall be copper alloys, brasses, or bronzes that meet the corrosion resistance and pitting resistance specified in MSFC-STD-3029.
These materials shall also exhibit high resistance to SCC as defined by MSFC-STD-3029.

Requirement: Copper alloys shall not be used in solutions with ammonium ions or in contact with ammonia to prevent SCC.
Model issues: The condition for 'solutions with ammonium ions' needs a specified concentration or range to be verifiable.
How to verify: Inspect material specifications and chemical compatibility reports against the defined usage conditions.
Suggested rewrite:
Copper alloys shall not be used in solutions containing ammonium ions above <<concentration>> to prevent SCC.
Copper alloys shall not be used in contact with ammonia to prevent SCC.

Requirement: Machining, grinding, and finishing operations on beryllium and beryllium alloys shall be performed either wet, using a liquid coolant with local ventilation, or dry, using high-velocity, close-capture ventilation.
Model issues: The requirement bundles two distinct operational modes (wet vs. dry) that need separate verification criteria.
How to verify: Inspect the process setup to confirm the specified coolant, ventilation, or dry setup is in use for the operation.
Suggested rewrite:
Machining, grinding, and finishing operations on beryllium and beryllium alloys shall be performed wet using a liquid coolant and local ventilation.
Machining, grinding, and finishing operations on beryllium and beryllium alloys shall be performed dry using high-velocity, close-capture ventilation.

Requirement: Tin solder and tin plating shall be alloyed with at least 3% lead to prevent the growth of tin whiskers.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a specific testable criterion for 'alloyed with at least 3% lead'; it needs a measurable specification for the composition.
How to verify: Analyze a sample of the solder and plating using chemical analysis to confirm the lead content meets or exceeds 3%.
Suggested rewrite: The tin solder and tin plating shall contain a lead content of at least 3%.

Requirement: For critical GS, lot sampling shall be used to verify the presence of at least 3% lead.
Model issues: The threshold 'at least 3% lead' is ambiguous; it should specify the acceptance criteria (e.g., 'shall not exceed 3% lead' or 'shall contain at least 3% lead').
How to verify: Perform lot sampling and analyze the samples to confirm the lead concentration meets the specified criteria.
Suggested rewrite: For critical GS, lot sampling shall be used to verify the presence of lead at a concentration of <<target concentration>>.

Requirement: Elastomers shall be in accordance with MIL-HDBK-149.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a specific testable condition; compliance with a standard must be tied to a measurable property.
How to verify: Inspect the elastomer material against the documented specifications in MIL-HDBK-149.
Suggested rewrite: Elastomers shall meet all material specifications defined in MIL-HDBK-149.

Requirement: Elastomers shall operate within the parameters of a design service life, including the vendor-specified shelf life.
Model issues: The requirement lacks specific, measurable criteria for 'design service life' and 'vendor-specified shelf life'.
How to verify: Subject the elastomers to accelerated aging tests and measure property degradation against the specified limits.
Suggested rewrite: Elastomers shall maintain specified operational properties for a minimum of <<design service life>>. Elastomers shall not degrade before the vendor-specified shelf life of <<shelf life>>.

Requirement: Elastomers shall be cure-dated for tracking purposes.
Model issues: What specific tracking information must the cure date be associated with?
How to verify: Inspect the elastomer batch to confirm the cure date and associated tracking identifier are present.
Suggested rewrite: Elastomers shall be marked with a cure date traceable to <<tracking identifier>>.

Requirement: Elastomers shall not have a corrosive effect on other materials when exposed to conditions normally encountered in service.
Model issues: The term 'corrosive effect' is not quantifiable.; The phrase 'conditions normally encountered in service' is too vague.
How to verify: Expose elastomer samples to defined service conditions and inspect the materials for degradation according to established criteria.
Suggested rewrite: The elastomers shall not cause material degradation on <<list of materials>> when exposed to <<defined service conditions>>.

Requirement: When rubbers or elastomers are used at low temperatures, the ability of these materials to maintain the required elastomeric properties shall be verified by testing them at or below use temperature.
Model issues: The requirement is too vague regarding what 'required elastomeric properties' means and how they are measured.
How to verify: Test the material at the specified low temperature and measure the specified elastomeric property against the defined acceptance criteria.
Suggested rewrite: The material shall maintain <<specific elastomeric property>> when tested at or below <<use temperature>>.

Requirement: Composite materials used in GS shall be in accordance with MIL-HDBK-17, Volumes 1 through 5.
Model issues: The requirement does not specify *which* composite materials are used, only that they must conform to the standard.
How to verify: Inspect material certifications against MIL-HDBK-17, Volumes 1 through 5.
Suggested rewrite: Composite materials used in GS shall conform to MIL-HDBK-17, Volumes 1 through 5.

Requirement: Defects resulting from manufacturing shall be assessed through NDE techniques to meet the intent of 6.4.15.

Suggested rewrite: Defects resulting from manufacturing shall be assessed using NDE techniques as defined in <<reference to 6.4.15>>.

Requirement: Refractory concrete used for heat and blast protection of flame deflectors and other areas of the launch pad shall be in accordance with KSC-SPEC-P-0012.
How to verify: Inspect the material specifications and installation records against KSC-SPEC-P-0012.
Suggested rewrite: Refractory concrete used for heat and blast protection of flame deflectors and other areas of the launch pad shall be in accordance with KSC-SPEC-P-0012.

Requirement: Lubricants containing chloro-fluoro compounds shall not be used with aluminum or magnesium.
How to verify: Inspect the material safety data sheets or procurement specifications for the lubricants.
Suggested rewrite: Lubricants containing chloro-fluoro compounds shall not be used with aluminum or magnesium.

Requirement: Lubricants containing chloro-fluoro compounds shall not be heated above their maximum temperature rating.
How to verify: Inspect the material safety data sheet or component specification for the maximum temperature rating of the lubricant.
Suggested rewrite: Lubricants containing chloro-fluoro compounds shall not be heated above their maximum temperature rating.

Requirement: Lubrication of flared tube fittings shall be in accordance with KSC-SPEC-Z-0009.
Model issues: The requirement relies on an external document (KSC-SPEC-Z-0009) which, while potentially verifiable via inspection, is not self-contained and lacks a direct, testable pass/fail criterion without referencing that external standard.
How to verify: Inspect the lubrication application on the flared tube fittings against the criteria defined in KSC-SPEC-Z-0009.
Suggested rewrite: Lubrication of flared tube fittings shall conform to the specifications detailed in KSC-SPEC-Z-0009.

Requirement: Materials that are not expected to meet the design life requirements but must be used for functional reasons shall be identified as limited-life items in accordance with 4.2.2.2.
Model issues: The term 'identified as limited-life items' lacks a specific, measurable action or state to verify.
How to verify: Inspect the system documentation or configuration to confirm the identification of materials per section 4.2.2.2.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall identify materials not expected to meet design life requirements but required for functional reasons as limited-life items according to 4.2.2.2.

Requirement: Thin plastic films and tape materials used in GS shall be tested in accordance with and meet the requirements of the following for flammability, ESD, and hypergolic ignition/breakthrough characteristics, respectively, as appropriate for the application: NASA-STD-6001 (Test 1 and A.7) and MMA-1985-79.

Thin plastic films and tape materials used in GS shall be tested for flammability in accordance with NASA-STD-6001 (Test 1 and A.7).
Thin plastic films and tape materials used in GS shall be tested for ESD in accordance with MMA-1985-79.
Thin plastic films and tape materials used in GS shall be tested for hypergolic ignition/breakthrough characteristics in accordance with MMA-1985-79.

Requirement: For GS used in a humid environment, materials shall meet one of the following criteria or be identified in the design documentation along with any action required, such as periodic inspection, maintenance, or replacement of the material:

Requirement: Fusion welding of GSE shall meet all requirements for nonflight hardware in AWS D17.1, with the exception of pressure systems (see 5.2.13).

How to verify: Inspect the welding procedure and documentation against AWS D17.1 and section 5.2.13.
Suggested rewrite:
Fusion welding of GSE shall meet all requirements for nonflight hardware in AWS D17.1.
Fusion welding of GSE shall meet the requirements specified in section 5.2.13 for pressure systems.

Requirement: A welding procedure specification (WPS) that addresses each type of weld shall be prepared and qualified prior to the start of production welding.
Model issues: The term 'each type of weld' is too vague; it needs to specify the scope of weld types to be addressed.

Suggested rewrite: A welding procedure specification (WPS) shall be prepared and qualified for every specified weld type prior to the start of production welding.

How to verify: Inspect the production welding documentation to confirm M&P engineer approval prior to welding commencement.
Suggested rewrite: Prior to the start of any production welding, all WPSs and procedure qualification records (PQRs) shall be approved by an M&P engineer authorized by NASA.

Requirement: Prior to the start of production welding, each welder and welding operator shall be qualified.
Model issues: Qualification criteria for welders and welding operators are not specified.
How to verify: Inspect the welder and operator qualification records before production welding commences.
Suggested rewrite:
Each welder shall possess qualification documentation prior to starting production welding.
Each welding operator shall possess qualification documentation prior to starting production welding.

Requirement: Prior to the start of any production welding, all welder/welding operator performance qualification (WPQ) shall be approved by an M&P engineer authorized by NASA.
How to verify: Inspect the production welding records to confirm M&P engineer approval prior to welding commencement.
Suggested rewrite: Prior to the start of any production welding, all welder/welding operator performance qualification (WPQ) shall be approved by an M&P engineer authorized by NASA.

Requirement: Welds whose failure could cause personnel injury, damage to flight hardware, loss of mission, or major damage to a significant ground asset shall be classified and inspected as Class A welds.
Model issues: The term 'significant ground asset' needs a quantifiable definition or classification.
How to verify: Review the asset classification documentation to confirm the weld falls under the specified criticality level.
Suggested rewrite: Welds whose failure could cause personnel injury, damage to flight hardware, loss of mission, or damage to a ground asset classified as <<asset criticality level>> shall be classified and inspected as Class A welds.

Requirement: Welds whose failure could cause loss of function or improper performance shall be classified and inspected as Class B welds.
Model issues: The term 'loss of function or improper performance' is too vague and needs to be defined by a specific criterion or reference.
How to verify: Review the design documentation to confirm the classification criteria for welds causing <<specific loss of function or improper performance>>.
Suggested rewrite: Welds whose failure causes <<specific loss of function or improper performance>> shall be classified and inspected as Class B welds.

Requirement: Welds whose failure could not cause improper performance or a hazard to personnel shall be classified and inspected as Class C welds.
Model issues: The term 'improper performance' is too vague and needs to be defined in relation to system functionality.
How to verify: Review the design documentation and failure mode analysis to confirm the weld classification criteria.
Suggested rewrite: Welds whose failure does not cause a defined system performance degradation or a hazard to personnel shall be classified and inspected as Class C welds.

Requirement: Brazing of aluminum alloys shall meet the requirements of AWS C3.7M/C3.7.
Model issues: The requirement references an external standard (AWS C3.7M/C3.7) without specifying which specific requirements must be met, making it incomplete for verification.
How to verify: Inspect the brazed joint against the criteria specified in AWS C3.7M/C3.7.
Suggested rewrite: Brazing of aluminum alloys shall conform to the specific requirements detailed in AWS C3.7M/C3.7 regarding <<specific process parameters>>.

Requirement: Torch, induction, and furnace brazing shall meet the requirements of AWS C3.4M/C3.4, AWS C3.5M/C3.5, and AWS C3.6M/C3.6.
Model issues: The requirement bundles three distinct standards; it should be split into three separate requirements.
How to verify: Inspect the brazing process documentation against the specified AWS standards.
Suggested rewrite:
Torch brazing shall meet the requirements of AWS C3.4M/C3.4.
Induction brazing shall meet the requirements of AWS C3.5M/C3.5.
Furnace brazing shall meet the requirements of AWS C3.6M/C3.6.

Requirement: Subsequent fusion welding operations in the vicinity of brazed joints or other operations involving high temperatures that might affect the brazed joint shall be prohibited unless it can be demonstrated that the fixturing, processes, methods, and/or procedures employed will preclude degradation of the brazed joint.
Model issues: The condition for prohibition ('unless it can be demonstrated...') is too broad and lacks a specific, testable criterion for precluding degradation.
How to verify: Review the documented fixturing, processes, methods, and procedures against the specified degradation limits.
Suggested rewrite: Subsequent fusion welding operations in the vicinity of brazed joints or other operations involving high temperatures that might affect the brazed joint shall be prohibited unless the fixturing, processes, methods, and/or procedures employed demonstrate that the brazed joint degradation shall not exceed <<max allowable degradation>>.

Requirement: Brazed joints shall be designed for shear loading and, for structural parts, not be relied upon for strength in axial loading.
Model issues: The requirement bundles two distinct design constraints that should be separated.
How to verify: Review the design documentation to confirm shear loading requirements and axial load reliance constraints are met.
Suggested rewrite:
Brazed joints shall be designed to withstand specified shear loading.
For structural parts, brazed joints shall not be relied upon for strength in axial loading.

Requirement: The shear strength of brazed joints shall be evaluated in accordance with AWS C3.2M/C3.2.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a clear subject performing the action; it should state what *shall* be evaluated.
How to verify: Review the test plan to confirm that the shear strength evaluation procedure references AWS C3.2M/C3.2.
Suggested rewrite: The system shall evaluate the shear strength of brazed joints in accordance with AWS C3.2M/C3.2.

Requirement: For furnace brazing of complex configurations, such as heat exchangers and cold plates, destructive testing shall be conducted on preproduction brazed joints to verify that the brazed layer that extends beyond the fillet area is continuous and forms a uniform phase.
Rule findings: open-ended list: such as; passive voice: shall be conducted
Model issues: The term 'complex configurations' is too vague and should be replaced with a specific definition or scope.; The requirement bundles two distinct verification criteria: continuity and uniformity of the brazed layer.
How to verify: Perform destructive testing on preproduction brazed joints and inspect the brazed layer to confirm continuity and phase uniformity.
Suggested rewrite:
The system shall subject preproduction brazed joints of defined complex configurations to destructive testing.
This testing shall verify that the brazed layer extending beyond the fillet area is continuous.
This testing shall verify that the brazed layer extending beyond the fillet area forms a uniform phase.

Requirement: Brazing of pressure vessels shall be in accordance with ASME BPVC VIII.
Model issues: The requirement lacks a specific scope or context for the application of ASME BPVC VIII.
How to verify: Inspect the brazing procedure and documentation against the specified edition of ASME BPVC VIII.
Suggested rewrite: The brazing of pressure vessels shall comply with the requirements of ASME BPVC VIII, Edition <<Edition>>.

Requirement: Soldering of electrical connections not exposed to vibration or thermal cycling shall be in accordance IPC J-STD-001.
Model issues: The condition 'not exposed to vibration or thermal cycling' is a design constraint, not a verifiable requirement on the soldering itself; it should be separated or clarified.
How to verify: Inspect the soldered connections against the IPC J-STD-001 standard.

Requirement: Soldering of electrical connections exposed to vibration or thermal cycling shall be performed in accordance with IPC J-STD-001ES.

Requirement: For critical GS, lot sampling shall be used to verify the lead content.

How to verify: Review the process documentation to confirm that lot sampling is mandated for all specified critical GS.

Requirement: Soldering shall not be used for structural applications.
How to verify: Inspect the design documentation and manufacturing process to confirm no soldering is used for structural components.
Suggested rewrite: Soldering shall not be used for structural applications.

Requirement: Heat treatment of aluminum alloy parts shall meet the requirements of SAE AMS 2770, SAE AMS 2771, or SAE AMS 2772, as appropriate.

Requirement: Steel parts shall be heat-treated to meet the requirements of SAE AMS-H-6875 or SAE AMS 2759.

How to verify: Inspect the material certifications to confirm compliance with the specified standard.

Steel parts shall be heat-treated to meet the requirements of SAE AMS-H-6875.
Steel parts shall be heat-treated to meet the requirements of SAE AMS 2759.

Requirement: Heat treatment of titanium and titanium alloy parts shall meet the requirements of SAE AMS-H-81200.
Model issues: The requirement relies on an external standard, which is acceptable, but it lacks a specific scope or context for the system being reviewed.

Requirement: Heat treatment of nickel-based and cobalt-based alloy parts shall meet the requirements of SAE AMS 2774.

Heat treatment of nickel-based alloy parts shall conform to SAE AMS 2774.

Requirement: The nickel-aluminum interface in nickel-plated aluminum shall be protected from exposure to corrosive environments.

How to verify: Expose the nickel-aluminum interface to the specified corrosive environment for a defined duration and inspect for signs of degradation.
Suggested rewrite: The nickel-aluminum interface in nickel-plated aluminum shall resist corrosion when exposed to <<specific corrosive environment>>.

Requirement: Chromium plating shall be in accordance with SAE AMS 2460.

Requirement: Cadmium plating shall be in accordance with SAE AMS-QQ-P-416.

Requirement: Adhesives shall not have a corrosive effect on other materials when exposed to conditions normally encountered in service.
